nodeData.note: CC Antya 3.137 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Haridasa Thakura gives his new disciple two simple practices: chant constantly and serve Tulasi Devi. Maharaj glorifies Tulasi's position, insists that sixteen rounds is only the minimum, and unpacks Mahaprabhu's verse on humility through the grass and the tree. Questions bring out why a fallen but sincere person receives mercy while outward status counts for little. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Haridasa Thakura's instruction to his new disciple: constant chanting together with service to Tulasi, as the way to come to Krishna's shelter. The purport connects it with surrender.

Maharaj counts them: chant the holy name continuously, and serve Tulasi Devi by watering her and offering prayers. It is considered the simplest method. — “Very simple but powerful”

🎙 Maharaj at 12:27 (auto-transcript): “What is the instruction? Ones will chant the holy name of Krishna continuously. and render service to Tulsi Devi which is offering prayers and water only two things water, Tulsi Devi offer prayers to Tulsi Devi”

Simply to see Tulasi, water her, pray to her and bow down captures one for Krishna. She is that special.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:20 (auto-transcript): “To see Tulsi Devi Just to see Tulsi Devi Watering making prayers and offering obeisances sigma bulletin to see one is already captured for Krishna She is so special.”

Not only devotees worship Tulasi; even demons do.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:16 (auto-transcript): “She is worshipped even by demons. Not only devotees worship her. Demons also worship her. the prayer we sing every morning and Vrindavan what do we sing the last line the last line no no”

children.topic: She is the life of Krishna
children.note:
Maharaj asks what the last line of the Tulasi song sung every morning means, and explains her position: she is the life of Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:11 (auto-transcript): “when we sing what's the last line means what what is the meaning the life of Jamuna Tulsi is what Tulsi is Krishna so forth she is there”

He briefly tells a pastime in which Krishna was restless and searched everywhere until Tulasi was found, and Lakshmi Devi received a stern warning never to repeat her offence. That is Tulasi's position.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:13 (auto-transcript): “when Lakshmi Devi saw it with her Krishna lived the whole Vaikuntha, the whole Vaikuntha was abandoned, was searching for her everywhere, Krishna Jeevani, until Krishna discovered her, See, he was restless.”

Krishna accepts an offering when he sees a Tulasi leaf on it. Keep Tulasi living in your home and Narayana is present as physically as she is. — “anywhere where Tulsi Devi is, Narayana must be present.”

🎙 Maharaj at 19:30 (auto-transcript): “Offer anything to Krishna what have Tulsi Krishna done is. When Krishna sees Tulsi Devi, then he will eat it. Therefore, anywhere where Tulsi Devi is, Narayana must be present. Narayan is present You want Narayan to be present”

Citing Vrindavana dasa Thakura, Maharaj says we should stand before Tulasi Devi — and that is what Haridasa did.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:35 (auto-transcript): “Therefore, Shri Vindhavandash Thakur Ji says, we should stand before Tulsi Devi. And that is what Haridash Thakur did here. Vindhavandash Thakur has been asked for him. We are going on a procession. Kuchis, Kuchis is for Krishna. Krishna will not go there without Tulsi Devi…”

In Ratha-yatra and in Navadvipa parikrama Tulasi always goes in front, because her presence brings Krishna. He left her behind as a blessing so that people could reach him easily by worshipping her.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:07 (auto-transcript): “Kuchis, Kuchis is for Krishna. Krishna will not go there without Tulsi Devi in the front. I like the Rata Yatra, Tulsi Devi is better. In our Navadi Parikrama, Tulsi is always present, because her presence rings Lord Krishna, Krishna left her behind, for the blessing, people…”

Pray to Tulasi Devi and chant sitting before her, and success in japa is sure.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:10 (auto-transcript): “So, Haydash Thakurji says, we should pray for Tulsi Devi. We should pray for her. And she should pray for her. and when they are sitting in front of them they should have to do the mantra we are sure to be successful in our japa we will be able to do the japa Prabhupada is…”

children.topic: Tulasi: a pure devotee among us
children.note:
With her blessing the name becomes easy to chant; gazing at her during japa, pure love of God is sure.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:11 (auto-transcript): “The holy name becomes easy to chant. And if you gaze at her, while doing japa pure love of God is sure we are complaining of lacking association with pure devotees Tulsi Devi is what?”

children.topic: No pure association? She is here
children.note:

children.topic: Be conscious of who sits there
children.note:
Know that the one sitting before you is there for your benefit; this awareness is Krishna consciousness, and the heart becomes beautiful. — “To be conscious of what we are doing.”

Sixteen rounds is for the lazy; the strong chant always. — “So 16 is a minimum.”

Maharaj recalls the Gita's description of great souls always chanting Krishna's glories — always, not sometimes.

children.topic: Bible and Quran say the same
children.note:
Not only Vaishnava literature teaches this: the Bible calls for praising the Lord's name from the rising to the setting of the sun, and Islam speaks of chanting the beautiful names of Allah.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:29 (auto-transcript): “it is not only Harakrishna or Vaisnava literature that teaches other scriptures taught the same In the Bible you find From the rising of the sun To the setting Once you call the name of the Lord This is the Bible The most beautiful name of Allah”

Even Sukracarya, guru of the asuras and no devotee, says that faults in a sacrifice — wrong pronunciation and other errors — are corrected by chanting the Lord's name, and the sacrifice becomes perfect. So give full attention to chanting. — “All mistakes have been corrected.”

🎙 Maharaj at 29:43 (auto-transcript): “and Shukracharya and Shukracharya is not a devotee the guru of the Ashuras Ashura's guru are gurudev are he says in doing Jagya some mistakes are always there so we have mantra to chant after Jagya begging for forgiveness for all the offenses mistakes”
Mahaprabhu gave the mood for chanting in one verse. Maharaj asks how many points it contains and takes them one by one.

Step on grass and it bows; step off and it springs up again. We should be humbler still and remain low — not rising back up the moment pressure is removed.

The devotees in the room offer meanings for the tree, and Maharaj names the one he was waiting for: a tree exists for others.

Have you seen a mango tree eat mangoes? Trees, and devotees, stand for others, not themselves. — “Have you seen any fruit eating the fruit?”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:08 (auto-transcript): “Have you seen mango eating mango? Have you seen any fruit eating the fruit? No. Means what? The trees are standing for others, not for themselves. A devotee is standing for others.”

This is a principal quality of Giriraja: he exists only to give service. A tree gives fruit, medicinal leaves, oxygen and wood.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:04 (auto-transcript): “That is one of the principal qualities of Giraj. the only reason Giraj is existing is to give service Devotees are folks A tree is standing only for the others There is a tree standing for the mother to give it to the other. He gives the fruit.”

Cut a tree and it does not cry for help against the man it served for years. Even as firewood and charcoal it keeps cooking for others — selfless, and very humble. Be more tolerant than that.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:34 (auto-transcript): “What is humility? If you cut the tree, Does he complain? No. Okay, does he complain? But does he call for help? Please help me. Look at this wicked man. Expect no respect, but give it. Those who wait to be loved before loving will wait for eternity; give selflessly and it becomes your experience.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:34 (auto-transcript): “The second part is Amanina Manadena what does that mean amani means what we should not expect respect but we give we give the respect if we give respect what will happen we will get respect”

Everyone knows this verse, yet we do not chant this way, because we have not learned to apply it. We sing songs without knowing their meaning; study the meaning and be conscious of what we are doing.

One person is labelled a prostitute, another respectable — is that label what decides spiritual qualification?

She came with a deceitful intention and Haridasa knew it, yet she received mercy — though it is said a cheating disciple is cheated.

nodeData.note: CC Antya 3.138–139 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Haridasa Thakura leaves chanting, and his new disciple gives away all her possessions exactly as ordered. Maharaj draws out how money given for Krishna's service purifies the giver, why the collector must act like a postman who keeps nothing, and why a disciple should follow rather than reinterpret, with the stories of Satrajit and of Gaura Kisora dasa Babaji's would-be disciple. Maharaj calls the purport a powerful lesson. Srila Prabhupada introduced life membership knowing that people's businesses are not fully Krishna conscious.

Donations are taken not for the benefit of the one receiving them but for those who give. Because it is used for Krishna, the giver is purified.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:12 (auto-transcript): “taking money from people or getting donations from people and not for the benefit of the devotee who are receiving it, not for his benefit, for the benefit of those who are giving it. So, it is good for them to give.”

The collector must keep nothing for himself; whatever he takes, he shares in the giver's karma. — “not even a Paisa, even half a Paisa, not even in a dream”

A faithful, sincere servant, she did not doubt or reinterpret her spiritual master's order. — “He just followed it.”

nodeData.note: CC Antya 3.140–142 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The former prostitute follows Haridasa Thakura's example exactly and becomes a celebrated Vaishnava. Maharaj draws out the lesson that devotion depends on quality and on following the guru's standard, not on birth, and shows how Mahaprabhu placed great devotees in low families to prove it. In the questions he explains why the Bhagavatam still glorifies qualified brahmanas, and how to make our chanting grow when it feels stuck at sixteen rounds. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: These verses describe how the woman sent to tempt Haridasa Thakura now lives as his disciple in his own room, chanting day and night, and becomes so advanced that great Vaishnavas come to see her.
This verse is about her daily discipline in the footsteps of her guru: worship of Tulasi, very simple eating, and the senses brought under control.
This verse tells how she became a famous devotee, visited by advanced Vaishnavas; the purport draws from it that a Vaishnava is judged by practice, not by origin.

Maharaj goes back over the verses: the key phrase is that she chanted and worshipped Tulasi following her spiritual master. That was the whole secret of her success, and why stalwarts came to see a devotee, not a prostitute.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:51 (auto-transcript): “The lesson to learn here is the character of the Spirit to do it. It is said here, Following in the footsteps of our spiritual master, she began chanting the holy name 300,000 times a day. She worshipped the Tulsi plant, falling in the full shape of her spiritual master.”

We may not chant three lakh names, but the mood and attitude of the guru must be followed. Quantity can differ; the standard cannot, and that is how mercy comes. — “But the standard has to be followed”

🎙 Maharaj at 09:48 (auto-transcript): “we may not chant 300,000 but the mood the attitudes we follow The standard should be followed The quantity may be different But the standard has to be followed That is how the mercy will come true”

She did not invent her own style of chanting; she copied her guru, and therefore she was purified very quickly. — “She chanted as the Guru chanted.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:37 (auto-transcript): “She didn't chant the way she wanted. She chanted as the Guru chanted. Therefore, she became quickly purified. So, Prabhupada said, anyone can become purified. It can be turned into a Vaisnawan.”

As Srila Prabhupada said, anyone can be purified and become a pure devotee, from any level of life, simply by following the principle.

Krishna is the father of all living beings, so the way to reach him is the same for everyone. What counts is quality, not the family one is born in.

🎙 Maharaj at 11:48 (auto-transcript): “Because Krishna is the supreme father for all living entities. Haridasa Thakura was Lord Brahma, yet he was sent into a Yavana family, and the Lord made him the namacarya, the teacher of the holy name.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:00 (auto-transcript): “Harada Sakura is formerly Lord Brahma Krishna sent him to Yagwana family When he came He brought him And made him Nama Chariya In his street we have a Brahmana Who chanted 300,000 names like Harida in history? Anyone? Mahabharata, Ramayana, any Puranas?”

Narottama Dasa Thakura was not born a brahmana, though he is an expansion of Nityananda Prabhu; and brahmanas took initiation from him into Vaishnava life.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:36 (auto-transcript): “Brahmana, but who is Narutam Dastakura? Expansion of Nityananda Prabhu. So, Nityananda Prabhu Nityananda Prabhu is a sutra. Nityananda Prabhu is a sutra. He is a supreme position of God. So his expansion is what? Sutra. Narottam Dasa Kura is an expansion of Lord Nityananda…”

Even Vyasadeva, an incarnation of Krishna, had a brahmana father and a mother from a lower family. Krishna is teaching that anyone can become a Vaishnava by following the discipline.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:42 (auto-transcript): “Shri La Vyafadeo Ji Vyashadeo His father is a Brahmana His mother is a Shudra But He is an incarnation of Krishna Krishna is teaching the superior nature of Vaishnava Krishna is teaching Vaishnava Vaishnava anyone can become”

children.topic: Three lakh names: no brahmana did
children.note:

🎙 Maharaj at 15:28 (auto-transcript): “Who chanted 300,000 names like Harida in history? Anyone? Mahabharata, Ramayana, any Puranas? Any Puranas? Any Puranas? Any Puranas chanted 300,000 names? Any Puranas? We don't have. Only Haridas Who is not a Brahmana He was not a Brahmana He was not a Brahmana Not only…”

And the woman, who had never practised spiritual life in this birth, at once chanted the same three lakh names as her spiritual master.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:12 (auto-transcript): “He was not a Prostitute He also chanted 300,000 names She had never practiced any spiritual life before She had never practiced any spiritual life before This is just the beginning And she was able to chant the same way as her special master chanted 300,000 names. What does…”

What does that mean? Her chanting did not begin here. One who never chanted in past lives will not take up the Hare Krishna mantra in this one. — “This is not the beginning.”

🎙 Maharaj at 16:43 (auto-transcript): “What does that mean for us? This lady has chanted in her past life. This is not the beginning. said. One who have never chanted Vasudeva in his past life will never chant Hare Krishna mantra this lifetime. So she is chanting 300,000 names. No Brahmana ever did. One hundred…”

The process is not to follow mechanically, but to follow exactly as our acaryas did; then we will be successful. — “One should not mechanically follow anything.”

🎙 Maharaj at 20:07 (auto-transcript): “So we should understand this process. One should not mechanically follow anything. We should follow exactly as our child has did. And we will be successful. Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Kisi ka koi prashna hai Koi tippadi hai Puh sakte hai Go in preampi”

children.topic: Q1 · Why does Bhagavatam glorify brahmanas?
children.note:
The Bhagavatam is meant for Kali-yuga, and we know brahmanas have fallen from their position — so why does it praise them in so many places?

🎙 Question from the floor at 21:06 (auto-transcript): “Shri Gurudev I just wanted to understand one thing Like since we know Shri Mat Bhaagotam That is Especially For us Shri Mat Bhaagotam Especially meant for this age, like how Krishna descended and even Bhagavatam came. Especially meant for this Kali Yuga, age of Kali Yuga. So…”

children.topic: The head of the social body
children.note:
Vedic culture divides society like a body: vaisyas the stomach, ksatriyas the arms, brahmanas the head, where the most important senses sit. The eyes are not on the feet.

🎙 Maharaj at 22:19 (auto-transcript): “Vedic culture divided the society into four social and four spiritual So, Brahman's position is high Vaishya, the stomach. Vaishya, the stomach. Chhatriya, the hands.”

The fool is peaceful and so is the one above the modes. The brahmana's peace comes from full knowledge of the Absolute, theoretical and realised — and like this devotee, he is clean, austere and straightforward. — “Ignorant can be peaceful”

🎙 Maharaj at 24:00 (auto-transcript): “Two kinds of people are peaceful in this world A foolish number one person is full, he is peaceful Ignorant can be peaceful And one who is above the three modes of nature So, the Brahman's peacefulness is not ignorance due to spiritual qualities. He is peaceful because he has…”

Maharaj recalls a lecture of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati praising the high place of brahmanas: the other orders depend on others, but the qualified brahmana stands on his own qualities.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:01 (auto-transcript): “One time, Bhakti Shiddhantra Ji was called for a lecture. So he went to the class. And in a lecture. unhowne brāhmaṇo ke guñnoka bhaqan ka na suru kiya ki brāhmaṇo log is samaj ka sir hain unka pad bhaoghut ucch hain krishna brāhmaṇo ke mokh se bhujan karta hai e kathah mein…”

Maharaj tests the room: who is free of anxiety, fully self-controlled, with senses depending on us rather than us on them? No hands go up — heads go down. He points to Narada's thirty qualities in the Bhagavatam's seventh canto, which Prabhupada wanted every human being to develop, and which they studied last year in Lagos with Sivarama Swami's explanations.

The real brahmana is a devotee. When the culture decayed, men became brahmanas by name only — brahma-bandhus, friends of brahmanas — and condemned qualified Vaishnavas. Narottama, Visvanatha, Baladeva and Srila Prabhupada worked hard to dismantle that ignorance, which is why we can sit here today.

🎙 Maharaj at 32:06 (auto-transcript): “A Brahman by name, not a quality. That is the point in discussion, not a qualified Brahman who is a devotee, but adulterated People who are not devotees, who are not bhaishnawars, Prabhupada called them Brahma Bandhu. One who is born in a Brahmanic family but is not…”

A devotee went from one round to two and slowly to sixteen, but now cannot go further. How does the taste and strength for chanting increase?

🎙 Question from the floor at 35:15 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Maharaj. Maharaj, we have seen in my case, I started with one round and two round. And then slowly I went to 16 rounds. But now 16 rounds is stuck. I'm not going up. I'm not able to go up. And where this spiritual strength comes, and this attraction for chanting…”

In the office we work like a donkey and get promoted when our service pleases the directors. Do we chant with that seriousness? Promotion in Krishna consciousness is chanting becoming sweeter and sweeter. — “Are we chanting like a donkey?”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:18 (auto-transcript): “In a secular world, material world, When we are working in office, how do we get promotion? How do we get promotion in office? Working like a donkey. We work like a donkey. Are we chanting like a donkey?”

Forget the three lakh — did Haridasa chant while using a phone or talking? He had full faith that the name and Krishna are the same. Is it respect to chant with a cell phone, or to plan our day while chanting?

🎙 Maharaj at 38:20 (auto-transcript): “how Haridah Sakur was chanted forgot about 300 Haridah was chanting and using his cell phone? Haridas. Haridas. Who was chanting and using his cell phone? No. Are we chanting with that mood? Haridas.”

Do we feel this? The holy name is a direct line to the Supreme Lord, so I cannot afford to chant badly. Let us cultivate that mood. — “I am the most fortunate person in the universe.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:02 (auto-transcript): “I am the most fortunate person in the universe. Do we have that feeling? Is that what we feel? I am the most fortunate person in the universe. because I have direct connection with the Supreme Lord direct is the holy name direct or indirect direct”

The questioner says this mood is too high for him. Maharaj recalls that when Haridasa told the woman to give away all her property, she did not protest. 'I want to, but not now' is already defeat. — “if you want to do it, do it”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:16 (auto-transcript): “Haidash Thakpur said go and sell all your properties give it to the Brahmanas and come back here did he protest she protested this is too difficult Guru De, I want to do it, but, but, but, but, but, but means what, but, what does it mean, but,”

nodeData.note: CC Antya 3.143 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Everyone glorifies Haridasa Thakura when they see the transformed prostitute, and Maharaj explains that a guru is known by the fruit of his disciples. Her secret was simple: she heard the instruction and carried it out at once, like the hunter whom Narada Muni turned into a Vaishnava. In the questions he discusses readiness for a guru, initiation taken under pressure, instructions one feels unable to follow, and the difference between imitating and following. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: This verse is about the onlookers' astonishment at the woman's transformation, and how it led them to honour Haridasa Thakura.

Phalena pariciyate: a tree is recognised by its fruit. Haridasa's greatness is seen in what he made of a professional prostitute. — “by the fruit a tree is known”

🎙 Maharaj at 00:35 (auto-transcript): “Also it is said by the fruit a tree is known. who is fortunate will make others fortunate a pure deity must make others pure Haridash Thakur has transformed the prostitute.”

One who is fortunate makes others fortunate; one who is pure must purify others. Changing a prostitute into a Vaishnava is Haridasa's quality.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:42 (auto-transcript): “who is fortunate will make others fortunate a pure deity must make others pure Haridash Thakur has transformed the prostitute.”

Haridasa chanted three lakh names, ate frugally and chanted with full absorption — and so did she, point for point. That likeness is the proof of a bona fide guru and a bona fide disciple.

🎙 Maharaj at 01:52 (auto-transcript): “Harada Sakura was chanting 300,000 names. The prostitute also was chanting 300,000 names. Harada was eating frugally, the disciple also was eating frugally. Haidash was chanting with full absorption, without destruction.”

She was given an instruction and did not argue; she simply did it, and therefore she succeeded.

🎙 Maharaj at 03:08 (auto-transcript): “The instruction was given to her. She did not protest. She did not agree about it. She followed it. Therefore she became successful.”

We receive instructions every day, but without practice the woman's experience will not become ours. — “Simply to hear from this spiritual master is not enough”

🎙 Maharaj at 04:02 (auto-transcript): “Simply to hear from this spiritual master is not enough, one more practices. A few years ago, a friend invited me to there. I went there with three disciples at the end.”

children.topic: 'Is any disciple doing what you do?'
children.note:
Invited to a program with three disciples, Maharaj was asked whether any of his disciples does what he does. He looked at them and honestly said no. He asks devotees how many of the things they ask him to speak about they actually follow — should the guru speak and the disciples not follow?

🎙 Maharaj at 04:09 (auto-transcript): “A few years ago, a friend invited me to there. I went there with three disciples at the end. They were asking me questions. One of the questions was asked was,”

children.topic: Sell everything — she went at once
children.note:
Told to sell her property and give it to brahmanas, she did not ask why after working so hard for it; she went immediately, distributed everything and came back.

🎙 Maharaj at 07:14 (auto-transcript): “Haridash Thakur gave instructions. Go and sell all your properties and distribute them to the Brahmanas, and you come back here. Why? Why? I worked very hard to get this facility. Why should I sell them? She didn't say that. Immediately she went and sold everything,…”

Scripture declares that everything is revealed only to one with unflinching faith in both guru and Krishna — and that is the bona fide disciple.

🎙 Maharaj at 08:11 (auto-transcript): “That is what the scripture declared One who has Unflatting faith in Guru and Krishna Only that disciple will get everything revealed. This same bona fide disciple. so Haridash Thakura said”

He told her to sit before Tulasi and chant without going anywhere, and left without saying when he would return. She did not worry; only his words were in her mind. Carrying an order on one's head means executing it, and then transformation follows. — “She carried the instructions of her Guru on her head.”

🎙 Maharaj at 08:52 (auto-transcript): “so Haridash Thakura said you sit here and chant the holy name before Torsi don't go anywhere she took the beads and chant it as Haridash Thakura said And as the Guru-Dev said to him, he was going to do it. He was a shraddha. And the Guru-Dev went and left him with his foot.…”
The same thing happened when Narada Muni delivered a professional hunter.

Narada told him to break his bow and arrows. The hunter asked how he would live, since hunting was the only trade his father gave him. Narada said: do it first, then come back. He obeyed without doubt or speculation. — “He followed him with faith.”

🎙 Maharaj at 10:41 (auto-transcript): “He told the hunter, break your bow and arrows and throw them away. He submissively inquired, my father did not give me any other profession than this hunting. So if I travel with these professions How will I maintain myself?”

Narada gave him the maha-mantra and promised to supply his needs. The hunter was not anxious about the future; the guru's instruction was the only thing in his life, and the news spread that the dangerous hunter had become a Vaishnava.

🎙 Maharaj at 12:03 (auto-transcript): “And when he came back, after breaking the balls and the arrows, after breaking the balls and the arrows, Narajji has given him the same Hare Krishna Mahamad You sit here and chant Here sit and sit in the name of Tulsi Devi And I will supply all your needs He followed it…”

children.topic: Food for life in the forest
children.note:
Cultured people never go to a sadhu empty-handed, so so much food arrived for one man that Maharaj jokes he started Food for Life.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:29 (auto-transcript): “People came to see him and cultural people They don't go to sadhu with empty hands. They were coming, woodily, short time. The bogger room was created. One person. How much will he eat? He started food for life. Yes, when Narajji came back, he came with his friends, and the…”

When Narada returned with his friend, the disciple ran to meet him zig-zagging — the man who once enjoyed leaving animals to die in pain was now checking the ground at every step.

🎙 Maharaj at 14:03 (auto-transcript): “Yes, when Narajji came back, he came with his friends, and the disciples showed the Guru was coming distance, he was running to go and meet the Guru, and he was turning zig-zaggy, Why? A dangerous hunter who takes pleasure in many animals who are dead so they die in pain.”

Parvata Muni was not surprised: Narada's touch can turn anyone into a pure devotee. The disciple's faith in the guru's word shows itself in the disciple's transformation.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:06 (auto-transcript): “Parvatamuni saw that he saw his friend I am not surprised you are a toast you can transform anything into pure devotee let us see what is happening the faith of the disciple in the word of the spiritual master will manifest in transforming the disciple”

Maharaj wants the same story to repeat in our own lives by following the instructions of the spiritual master.

🎙 Maharaj at 15:53 (auto-transcript): “Let history repeat in our own lives that we should follow the instructions of the special master. We get messages every day. Guru Deo, I am not able to follow your instructions. As a disciple, three days ago, a devotee wrote me,”

A devotee wrote asking a question while already apologising in advance in case he did not follow the answer — defending himself before any instruction was given. Compare that with the prostitute and the hunter.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:34 (auto-transcript): “As a disciple, three days ago, a devotee wrote me, Please, please, don't be offended if I don't follow your instructions on the questions I am asking you. He's asking me a question without my answer. He's already prepared for defense. I know you're going to give me heavy…”

Others come wanting instruction but asking him not to push. If you already know the solution, why ask anyone?

🎙 Maharaj at 17:45 (auto-transcript): “some years ago a good brother came to me I want to get an instruction for you. Please, don't tell me too fast. If you know the solution to your problem, why do you have to go to somebody? Recently, this one was already the same thing to me. Please, I am going to ask you…”

Asking the guru about something one has no intention of doing is an offence. Let the guru's potency work by following what he says. — “Don't ask the questions for things you are not ready to do.”

🎙 Maharaj at 18:56 (auto-transcript): “It is an offense. You have to ask a special master for something that you cannot do. Don't ask the questions for things you are not ready to do. Let the Guru's potency manifest in our lives. It should allow him to transform us by following the instructions.”

Pure devotees are soft-hearted toward disciples and instruct according to each one's nature, just as a doctor prescribes for a particular illness. We must take the medicine as prescribed.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:56 (auto-transcript): “So, the Prophet said, pure devotees, their heart is very soft towards the disciples. Therefore, they give instruction based on our own nature and it is for our own benefit. Doctors do not just give medicines, they give medicines according to our disease, and it should help us…”

children.topic: Go to a guru when ready
children.note: Tasmad gurum prapadyeta: go to a guru when you sincerely want the highest good and are ready to hear his answer — not for fashion.

children.topic: A guru is seen through disciples
children.note:
People came to see the woman and saw the guru in her. As a citizen's acts are credited to the king, a disciple's acts go to the guru, so both must be bona fide. — “A guru is seen through his disciples.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:42 (auto-transcript): “people came to see the woman they saw the guru to the disciple A guru is seen through his disciples. All the activities of disciples goes to the guru. All the activities of a citizen go to the king.”

Four questions on readiness, initiation, hard instructions and imitation.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:57 (auto-transcript): “Thank you for this very wonderful lesson. My question is related to the last part of class today. And that is about when is a disciple really ready to accept a spiritual master? When is a disciple really ready to accept the shelter of a spiritual master? So we see that we are…”

We come to a guru precisely because we are weak and want to change, and faith itself comes from the guru — so what does it mean to be ready?

🎙 Question from the floor at 25:11 (auto-transcript): “My question is related to the last part of class today. And that is about when is a disciple really ready to accept a spiritual master? When is a disciple really ready to accept the shelter of a spiritual master? So we see that we are coming to the spiritual master because we…”

Coming while knowing one is weak is fine. Going to a doctor means admitting I am sick and cannot cure myself; having been diagnosed, the next step is to take the medicine.

🎙 Maharaj at 27:20 (auto-transcript): “When a bhakti comes to the spiritual master, knowing fully well that I am very weak, that's okay. If I don't feel I'm sick, I'm going to go to the doctor. Going to the doctor means that I'm convinced that I'm sick. And I cannot cure myself. Many guilty people who can”

Maharaj acts out the patient bargaining down the dose because he is so weak. Since we made the effort to reach the doctor, we should make the effort to take the medicine. — “Can I take one pill once a week?”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:46 (auto-transcript): “Oh, doctor, you know I am very, very weak. That seems nice. You know I am very weak. Can I take one pill once a week? Doctor. Doctor. One. One. One. Two. Two.”

children.topic: Put the mercy in my mouth
children.note:
Some keep returning to say the sickness is still there without taking the medicine, and want the merciful doctor to do it for them.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:41 (auto-transcript): “What do we want the doctor to do? You are so merciful, you are so compassionate, you are so compassionate, can't you do put the mercy in my mouth, you are so compassionate but I have to take the trouble to take the Don't put it in my mouth. Some of us are like this.”

If we are given instructions and do not follow them, we have no right to complain. The prostitute did not behave like that; Prabhupada's purport says twice that she followed in her guru's footsteps.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:29 (auto-transcript): “One day I had to tell one day what is it? What is the right to complain? You have been given instructions, do like this. You are not doing it. And I complain it. What is your rights? This prostitute did not do like that. Shri Prabhupada has said that twice in two slogans. And…”

children.topic: Q2 · Initiated before I was ready
children.note:
A devotee says many, herself included, were pushed to take initiation within a year or two without real determination. She is grateful, and ready now — how to close the gap?

🎙 Question from the floor at 32:46 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, thank you very much for the class. So much inspired to hear how much we need to have determination when we approach it to the Guru. And I'm thinking, I've seen very few devotees like that in my surroundings who, before taking initiation, had that much determination.…”

Those pushed into a decision should now learn the process properly, correct the mistakes they were pushed into, and seek help from someone experienced.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:21 (auto-transcript): “Yes, for those who are pushed to take decision without understanding what we are going in for, So, we have really pushed in there. Now we should start to learn the process nicely.”

Outside the Krishna-Balarama guest house a devotee cried at having been forced to take initiation from someone they felt no connection with. Maharaj said that was all right: take shelter of the one they do feel connected with, continue, and be happy.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:05 (auto-transcript): “I remember in the front of a Kishnabalama guest house, a devotee came to me crying I was forced to take initiation from this person I had no connection with that person so I told the person that is okay now you are ready in that that is okay But the person you have in their…”

If we take initiation and then misbehave, break our vows and keep no connection with the spiritual master, Krishna may take that guru away early. So we must rectify ourselves and start following nicely.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:10 (auto-transcript): “And for those of us who have delivered me, made our choice, and are not falling, which is wrong, it will be very dangerous, and it will be very dangerous. if we take initiation and are not folding and are not misbehaving and are not misbehaving and breaking the pressure and…”

children.topic: Q3 · An instruction I cannot follow
children.note:
What if the guru gives an instruction the disciple cannot follow — for example, to become a pure devotee?

🎙 Question from the floor at 41:04 (auto-transcript): “One question was asked, what if a disciple asked something from the spiritual master and the spiritual master gives instruction which he cannot follow? For example, that devotee who asked the spiritual master to become a pure devotee or something of that sort, that disciple…”

Maharaj contrasts an unauthorised guru who had a disciple sell his house and hand over the money, leaving the family with no future, with Haridasa, who gave the woman a place and a practice before Tulasi. A disciple should know which instructions are bona fide.

🎙 Maharaj at 42:09 (auto-transcript): “In the morning of Krishnamal Lam Mandir in the morning of the class, I know one guru, he told his disciple, He said, sell your house, give me the money, and that he said who did it, as foolishness.”

What else should a guru expect? We took a spiritual master, not a sports coach, and the agreement is to go back to Godhead. So thank him, ask what to do to become pure, and if unclear inquire submissively. — “We say spiritual master. We don't say football master.”

🎙 Maharaj at 45:07 (auto-transcript): “So if a disciple tells a guru, I want you to be a pure devotee. If a guru tells a disciple, I want you to be a pure devotee. Is that not what the Guru should expect from the disciples? Is it not? What is a Guru expecting from a disciple? To remain here in the material world?…”

What is the difference between imitating the guru and following in his footsteps?

🎙 Question from the floor at 48:59 (auto-transcript): “My question is, what's the difference between imitation and following the footsteps of the Guru? Tomorrow morning, from tomorrow morning, I will take only juice. That is what my Guru is doing.”

Deciding to take only juice because my guru does, and giving up after three days, is imitation — playing drama like a guru.

🎙 Maharaj at 49:29 (auto-transcript): “Tomorrow morning, from tomorrow morning, I will take only juice. That is what my Guru is doing. That is imitation. Because you are not going to do it more than three days. You are not going to do it more than three days. following that is a mutation”

children.topic: Doing what he asks of me
children.note:
Following means doing what he instructs us: we were initiated to chant, he asks us to become pure devotees, and we take up whatever process he gives for that.

🎙 Maharaj at 50:36 (auto-transcript): “My Guru chants a six-round before taking prasada. Let me do like it. My Guru reads a six-round and a six-round. They are chants a six-round. I have to do this in a day. That is for me. we took initiation for that to chant that is following we tell us to become a pure devotee…”

nodeData.note: CC Antya 3.144–165 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The seed of Ramacandra Khan's offence against Haridasa Thakura grows into a tree and bears fruit: he insults Lord Nityananda, and a Muslim official ruins him and his whole village. Maharaj warns how devastating offence to a devotee is, lists the six grave offences, and in the questions speaks about leaders who correct out of love, conflicts fed by false ego, and not carrying resentment into our japa. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: This verse describes Ramacandra Khan's plot with the prostitute as a seed of offence at Haridasa's feet that grows into a tree and later bears fruit for him to eat.

Maharaj loves the analogy. The seed is the selfish intention; the tree grows as we plan and carry out the deed; the fruit is the result that comes once the act is done. — “Everything has a beginning.”

🎙 Maharaj at 03:50 (auto-transcript): “Very beautiful analogy. Very beautiful. Everything has a beginning. It begins from the end. Then the seed is planted. The seed is the intention or desire. when the selfish desire”

We think we will enjoy the fruit, but from sinful seeds only suffering comes. Now Ramacandra Khan begins to taste his.

🎙 Maharaj at 06:24 (auto-transcript): “We will be enjoying the fruits. In the times of sinful seeds, it's always suffering that comes. So Ramachandra Khan will start enjoying the fruit of his sinful earth.”

children.topic: Ramacandra Khan becomes like an asura
children.note: The next verses describe Ramacandra Khan as a non-devotee by nature who, after offending Haridasa and long blaspheming Vaishnavas, becomes demoniac; the purport compares him with Ravana, born of a brahmana yet an asura through his offences.
These verses tell how Lord Nityananda, touring Bengal to preach and to subdue the faithless, comes to Ramacandra Khan's Durga-mandapa with many followers, and how he is turned away.

The purport here distinguishes the devotee who worships quietly from the one who also preaches and defeats atheism, as Nityananda did on Mahaprabhu's order.

🎙 Maharaj at 13:36 (auto-transcript): “There are two classes of devotees. One is called Gosyanandi, and the other is called Vajlanandi. A devotee who does not preach but always engages in devotional activities is called Vajlanandi. Whereas a devotee who not only is an expert in devotional activities, but who also…”

Staying inside with his family, Ramacandra Khan sends a servant to tell Nityananda to lodge elsewhere, perhaps with a cowherd; Nityananda laughs, agrees the place is fit only for cow-killers, and leaves the village.

🎙 Maharaj at 20:29 (auto-transcript): “The servant informed on it, My Jaisa Ramachandrakhan has sent me to accommodate you in some common man's house. You might go to the house of a milkman.”

Ramacandra Khan has the earth where Nityananda sat dug out and the mandapa smeared with cow dung, still not satisfied.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:00 (auto-transcript): “Ramachandra Khanna Seva ka agya dila Gosandiyan Vasilatarmati Kordailan Ramachandra Khanna Namakar ko agya dhi Ki jahaan per Nityanand Bhu baihthe thay Us isthaan ki mitti ko Nikal ke khoj daalo Ramachandra Khanna Order the servant to dig up The dirt in the place We are in…”

Because he had evaded the government's taxes, a Muslim minister comes, stays in that very Durga-mandapa, cooks a cow there for three days, arrests the family and plunders the house and village.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:39 (auto-transcript): “Ramachandra Khan's missionary was questionable, for he tried to avoid paying income tax to the government. Therefore, the government minister of finance was angry and came to his residence as he said durga mandapi basa koila abadya vata kari man sasigari randi”

children.topic: One man's fault, a whole village
children.note:
When an advanced devotee is insulted, the whole place suffers for one man's fault. Haridasa meanwhile walks on to Candapura and stays with Balarama Acarya.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:30 (auto-transcript): “However, an advanced devotee is insulted, for one man's fault, the entire town or place is afflicted. Haridash Thakur, chalte chalte, chandpur naama gaon mein aaye. Haridasa Kura walked until he came to the village known as Chandapura.”

Ramacandra's offence ruins his entire village — that is how dangerous it is to offend.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:53 (auto-transcript): “The offense of Ramachandra is affecting the whole village. that is how dangerous it is”
From the Bhagavatam: Suruci offended Dhruva when he was a little prince. When Dhruva attained pure love of God the reaction appeared — Suruci died, her son Uttama died, and many Yaksas were killed.

Maharaj gives an analogy: sin is like dust, which you can clean with your hand; offence is like a hole torn in a boat, which no hand can stop. — “Offence is very devastating.”

🎙 Maharaj at 34:53 (auto-transcript): “Offence is very devastating. It's like Gorg Viddham Haran said. Offence is like torn a boat. and sin is like dust dust you can clean it with hand turn the board you cannot stop it with hand very destructive The surest way to go to hell is to offend the devotee.”

Offending a devotee is a certain road to hell that no one can block. — “The surest way to go to hell is to offend the devotee.”

🎙 Maharaj at 35:36 (auto-transcript): “The surest way to go to hell is to offend the devotee. No one can be stopped from going to hell. It is sure, one will go to hell, that is sure, that is said. Even if a devotee forgives, Krishna will not forgive.”

Even if the devotee forgives, Krishna takes action. So great care about offences is essential; there are many kinds — to the name, Vaishnavas, service, living beings, prasada, the dhama, the guru.

🎙 Maharaj at 36:16 (auto-transcript): “Even if a devotee forgives, Krishna will not forgive. He will take action. So, to be careful with making offenses is very, very necessary, very important. There are many types of offenses. Naam Aparat. Vaishnav Aparad, Seva Aparad, Jiva Aparad, Prasad Aparad, Dham Aparad,…”

Maharaj lists the six forms of the gravest offence against a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:31 (auto-transcript): “Seven, Parama Aparad, yes. is also six, just ten, ten, six, and all that. Paramaparad is six. One, not to be happy upon seeing a devotee. Two, even if one is happy to see a devotee and have covered obeisance externally, but in the mind, he is thinking, who is this person?”

children.topic: No joy on seeing a devotee
children.note:
The first is simply not to feel happy when one sees a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 37:56 (auto-transcript): “One, not to be happy upon seeing a devotee. Two, even if one is happy to see a devotee and have covered obeisance externally, but in the mind, he is thinking, who is this person? Why have you come here?”

The second: bowing outwardly while inwardly thinking, who is this, why has he come, how long will he be here?

🎙 Maharaj at 38:11 (auto-transcript): “Two, even if one is happy to see a devotee and have covered obeisance externally, but in the mind, he is thinking, who is this person? Why have you come here? How long are you going to be here? It's Paramahaparad. Three. To be angry with devotees.”

Then: being angry with devotees, envying them, planning to harm them subtly or grossly by words or deeds, and finally trying to kill a devotee.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:52 (auto-transcript): “Three. To be angry with devotees. Four. To envy a devotee. Five. To plan to enjoy a devotee. Either vaguely or grossly. Yodhana banana ki kaise iski ninda ki jaye, kaise isko kuch chon't paunchai jaye. Ya toh apne sabdoun se, ya sari rikroop se. Six. Chhathama. Ek bhakti ko…”

One does not suffer alone; generations of the family share in it — just as when one person becomes a pure devotee, generations are liberated.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:44 (auto-transcript): “what will not suffer each alone. Generations of our family members will participate. Just as if one person becomes a pure devotee. Generations of family members will be liberated. So, what is there? Hare Krishna. Comments.”

Questions on the story and on offences in a family line.

🎙 Maharaj at 40:26 (auto-transcript): “Comments. Yes. Thank you for the lecture. I'm just wondering, there is any marriage in Chandra Khan? Because of him, Hari Vastakur has a disciple, of pure devotee and also we have the story that now we are talking about. Who is a devotee of her, yes. A prostitute.”

children.topic: Q1 · Any merit in Ramacandra Khan?
children.note:
Through him Haridasa gained a pure-devotee disciple — does Ramacandra Khan get any credit?

🎙 Question from the floor at 40:37 (auto-transcript): “Thank you for the lecture. I'm just wondering, there is any marriage in Chandra Khan? Because of him, Hari Vastakur has a disciple, of pure devotee and also we have the story that now we are talking about. Who is a devotee of her, yes. A prostitute.”

The merit is the prostitute's, who followed Haridasa and went back to Godhead. He sent her to ruin a saint; he dug up the ground where Nityananda sat, and Nityananda came only to punish him.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:23 (auto-transcript): “Ramachandra Khan has no merit. The prostitute has merits. She followed at the full serve of Haridasa and went back to Gaurav. Ramachandra Khan, what principle did he follow? he sent a prostitute to be delivered his intention was sinful”

Because of Hiranyakasipu, Lord Nrsimhadeva appeared for us to worship. From Ramacandra Khan nothing came; he ruined his life and his village.

🎙 Maharaj at 44:03 (auto-transcript): “Hiran Kashipu is different. Because of Hiran Kashipu, Lord Nasinghe Day appeared, we can worship. From Ramachandra Khan, what came out? What came out? Nothing? Raya Kashyapu, he probably sing a day for us to worship. He's important. Ramachandakhan, what is it?”

Our ancestors were not Vaishnavas. How would we know if offences were committed in the family — would service be interrupted, or chanting blocked?

🎙 Question from the floor at 46:54 (auto-transcript): “Yes. about the Vaishnava Prat which is committed in a family so the generations get the effect yes our ancestors were not any Vaishnavas how to know if in a Brahmin family there has been certain aparats that has happened what are the symptoms of that which we would have…”

It shows like a hereditary sickness — the doctor asks whether anyone in the family had it before. Some things have to be rectified in the family before life can move forward.

🎙 Maharaj at 48:11 (auto-transcript): “We will have a hereditary sickness. You are asthmatic, or all your children will be asthmatic? Asthma. Many other things like that.”

children.topic: Q3 · How can we stop offending?
children.note:
Offences seem so common in us that it feels impossible ever to be free. How do we actually stop?

🎙 Question from the floor at 51:18 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj Thank you for this wonderful class My question goes like this All the offenses are so common in us that even after having the idea of the glories of the holy name which will deliver us upon contemplating upon these offenses it seems like we will always be…”

children.topic: We suffer so that we cry
children.note:
Why do we suffer? So that we cry, please help me. If we stay comfortable, Krishna lets us continue; when we are tired of it and cry for mercy, he takes it out. — “You have to be tired of it and cry for mercy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 52:13 (auto-transcript): “Do you know why we are suffering? Why are we suffering? So that we cry. Please, please help me. Then Krishna will take it out.”

Three more questions on how devotees deal with one another.

🎙 Maharaj at 53:47 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj. Sometimes in our rational society, in the curve of management, in the cover of management, sometimes knowingly or unknowingly this aparath happens, avoid that thing. If the manager is not the manager of the leader,”

In managing a society, offences sometimes happen knowingly or unknowingly. How to avoid them?

🎙 Question from the floor at 53:48 (auto-transcript): “Sometimes in our rational society, in the curve of management, in the cover of management, sometimes knowingly or unknowingly this aparath happens, avoid that thing. If the manager is not the manager of the leader,”

A leader with character chastises followers when they go wrong; however it is received, he is not affected, because it is done out of love. A mistake made out of envy is paid for heavily.

🎙 Maharaj at 54:42 (auto-transcript): “A leader with character Who will chastise the followers for doing something wrong It may be received favorably or unfavorably, but that leader will not be affected.”

Every responsible leader must sometimes show anger, and that anger is love: if I did not care, I would not correct you. Pariksit, Prthu, Prabhupada and Maharaj's own gurus showed it, and for a fortunate disciple it purifies. — “Correcting is caring.”

🎙 Maharaj at 56:28 (auto-transcript): “Every responsible leader, most show anger sometimes. That anger is love, not anger actually. Because if we don't care for you, I won't correct it when you are doing something.”

How do we avoid offending devotees when we have differences of opinion?

🎙 Question from the floor at 58:38 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, how do we avoid committing our frances to devotees when there is difference of hope? Our question is that we will keep from this approach, from the approach of the approach, when we do not have a problem in two times, or we will keep ourselves from a situation and we…”

Unresolved conflict is kept alive by envy and false ego: I am superior, you keep quiet — and the other says the same, so there is a quarrel. — “Unresolved conflict is maintained by envy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 59:03 (auto-transcript): “Unresolved conflict is maintained by envy. Unresolved conflict. So if there is a problem and we have not done it, then we have kept our own faith in our own hands. False ego. resolve conflict, the base is fueled by falsy God.”

Maharaj turns to Prabhupada's purport on the Pracetas: since devotees share one occupation, serving Krishna, differences about service are spiritual. If they become a problem, we are leaning toward material things and showing false ego.

If a devotee behaves badly and we are disturbed by it, is that keeping them negatively in mind — and how do we keep them positively so we can chant?

🎙 Question from the floor at 66:53 (auto-transcript): “Thank you, Shilagurudev. Shilagurudev, I was thinking you mentioned in your previous classes that we cannot really chant the holy name if we keep anybody negatively in our mind. Yes. So there are just two parts to my question. first is if there is grossly offensive behavior…”

Yes, it is wrong, because we remember the person for the wrong they did. Even the Bible says not to take anger to bed — finish it before you sleep. How much more should a Vaishnava?

🎙 Maharaj at 69:33 (auto-transcript): “Even in the Bible, it is said, one should not take anger, disturbance to the bed. That means, we should finish it before we sleep.”

Carried day after day, these things pile up like dust a thousand kilometres thick on the heart; throw anything in and it is buried. When we sit to chant we may remember only the name.

🎙 Maharaj at 70:43 (auto-transcript): “As we continue to carry these things, they are accumulating and presently our situation is like the dots of our scene are like 150 kilometers, 1,000 kilometers. You may not see that in your heart, that is what it is, 1,000 km thick dust.”

The one who punched you has forgotten it; you carry it into your japa — Hare Krishna, you hit my face. Who is bad, the one who did it or the one keeping the garbage? We meditate so deeply on the problem that it becomes the deity of our heart, with no space left for Krishna. — “That is not japa.”

🎙 Maharaj at 73:34 (auto-transcript): “one who is keeping the garbage the person must have forgotten I have punched your face last night I am carrying the punches in my heart you have punched my face Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna He will punch my face. He will punch my face. And when we are doing japa, he will come.…”
